column1: # Share of each language's speakers living in each country, relative numbers
# normalised per row. This is what separates where a language is spoken from
# Only rows that need it are here. An entry left out is weighted by population
# alone, which is right whenever one country holds nearly all the speakers:
# Hindi is 100% India by population too, and German comes out DE 82 / AT 9 /
# CH 5 without help. pipeline.weights flags an entry when a second country
# takes 10% or more of the weight and no row exists here.
# THESE ARE ESTIMATES, not a cited source. No free dataset carries speakers per
# country; Ethnologue does and is paywalled. They are good to the nearest ten
# percent, which is all the scoring formula can use, since the weight only
# modulates an inside-score by plus or minus 40 percent. Correct any that look
# wrong on the reveal map, the effect is immediate.
